sentences.text: This appeal is filed against the judgment and award dated 03.09.2021 passed by the Senior Civil Judge and MACT- 11 , Aland, in MVC No.233 of 2020.
4. One Padmavati, wife of Shankar Kambar met with an accident on 24.02.2019 and died.
Her two sons and a daughter filed claim application claiming compensation of Rs.15,10,000/-.

The Tribunal,
considering the entire evidence on record, granted the compensation of Rs.4,70,040/- with interest at the rate of 6 percent per annum from the date of petition till realisation, and respondent No.3 was directed to deposit the said award amount within 30 days from the date of passing of the award.
5. Aggrieved by the said order, this appeal is filed by the appellant-insurance company mainly contending that insured NC: 2025:KHC-K:6617 HC-KAR vehicle was not involved in the accident.
It was falsely implicated in collusion with police.
Accident did not occur in the public place.
The owner allowed the vehicle to be driven by a person not holding valid driving licence and it is in violation of the provisions of M.V. Act and the insurance policy.

The deceased was an old woman, aged 90 years,
and therefore, the quantum granted by the Tribunal is very high and the claimants are entitled for the compensation towards loss of estate only.
6. Perusal of record shows that respondent Nos.1 to 3, including the appellant herein, remained ex-parte before the Tribunal and they had not raised any objection.
Admittedly, deceased was aged 90 years at the time of accident and the lowest multiplier of 5 was taken.

Her income was taken as Rs.8,000/- per month and the Tribunal granted loss of estate at Rs.3,20,040/- and also granted consortium and other conventional heads to the children and finally, granted the compensation of Rs.4,70,040/- with interest at the rate of 6% per annum from date of petition till realisation.
Therefore, as the appellant-insurance company herein had not contested the matter before the Tribunal, now it cannot raise all the NC: 2025:KHC-K:6617 HC-KAR objections at the appellate stage.
Therefore, this Court finds that there are no merits in the appeal and the appeal is liable to be dismissed confirming the award of the Tribunal.
7. Accordingly, the appeal is dismissed.
The impugned award passed by the Tribunal is hereby confirmed.
The appellant-insurance company has already deposited the awarded amount and therefore, the claimants are permitted to withdraw the said amount along with the accrued interest equally.
